nodes.label: Maximal Brain Damage Without Data or Optimization: Disrupting Neural Networks via Sign-Bit Flips
nodes.author: Ido Galil, Moshe Kimhi, Ran El-Yaniv
nodes.rationale: Exposes fundamental vulnerability in DNNs: flipping a small number of carefully selected sign bits can catastrophically degrade performance across vision, detection, segmentation, and reasoning LLMs without data or optimization.

nodes.label: Deep Neural Lesion (DNL) Attack
nodes.rationale: Data-free, optimization-free method identifying critical parameters via magnitude-based heuristics and early-layer targeting, enabling catastrophic model disruption through minimal bit flips.

nodes.label: 1P-DNL Attack (Single-Pass Variant)
nodes.rationale: Enhanced variant using single forward/backward pass on random inputs with hybrid importance scoring combining magnitude and gradient-based saliency for refined critical parameter selection.

nodes.label: Critical Parameters in DNNs
nodes.rationale: Parameters disproportionately vulnerable to bit flips, characterized by large magnitude and early-layer placement; vast majority of parameters remain robust to random perturbations.

nodes.label: Bit-Flip Attack Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Attacker has write access to stored parameters but no access to data or ability to run forward/backward passes; can flip small number of bits via rootkit, firmware, DMA, Rowhammer, or voltage glitching.

nodes.label: Magnitude-Based Parameter Selection
nodes.rationale: Heuristic targeting high-magnitude parameters for sign flips, inspired by pruning literature; simple yet powerful strategy for identifying critical parameters without optimization.

nodes.label: Early-Layer Targeting Strategy
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding that targeting early layers causes disproportionate damage due to error propagation through subsequent layers, analogous to neural lesions in biological systems.

nodes.label: One-Flip-Per-Kernel Constraint
nodes.rationale: CNN-specific heuristic constraining attacks to flip at most one bit per convolutional kernel, preventing cancellation effects where multiple flips within same kernel partially offset each other.

nodes.label: Selective Defense Using DNL
nodes.rationale: Defense mechanism protecting only most vulnerable sign bits identified by DNL using bit replication or error-correcting codes, substantially improving robustness with minimal overhead.

nodes.label: Optimal Brain Damage (OBD)
nodes.rationale: Classical pruning criterion using second-order Taylor expansion to identify important weights; theoretical foundation for magnitude and gradient-based parameter importance scoring.

nodes.label: Neural Network Pruning
nodes.rationale: Body of work on removing low-importance weights; provides theoretical and empirical insights into parameter importance that inform both DNL attack and defense strategies.

nodes.label: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Architecture
nodes.rationale: Architecture where each token routes through subset of experts; vulnerable to targeted bit flips in expert parameters despite sparse routing.

nodes.label: Rowhammer Attack
nodes.rationale: Hardware exploit exploiting DRAM disturbance errors to flip bits in adjacent rows; practical mechanism for executing DNL attacks.

nodes.label: DeepNcode Defense
nodes.rationale: Encoding-based defense using redundant codewords; vulnerable to DNL attacks through gray-box exploitation of decoding step.

nodes.label: Weight-Scaling Defense
nodes.rationale: Defense multiplying parameters by constant; ineffective against sign-flip attacks since sign flips are multiplicative perturbations.
